data.name: Bayram
data.gender_notes: Bayram is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who brings joy and delight to others. The name Bayram carries the meaning “Joy, Delight” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Turkish, Arabic. Parents who choose Bayram usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, delight and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Bayram belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, Delight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bayram total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: بيرم

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم بيرم مشتق من كلمة بيرم التي تعني العيد أو الاحتفال، ويرتبط بعيد الفطر أو عيد الأضحى في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية. يستخدم هذا الاسم في بعض البلدان الإسلامية للإشارة إلى هذه الأعياد المهمة.

in_urdu.name: بیرم
in_urdu.meaning: عید الفطر یا عید الاضحیٰ کے لئے استعمال ہونے والا نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: بیرم نام عربی زبان کے الفاظ سے ماخوذ ہے، جو عید یا تہوار کے معنی میں ہے۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں عید الفطر یا عید الاضحیٰ کے لئے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے، جو مسلمانوں کے لئے اہم مذہبی تعطیلات ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: बैरम
in_hindi.meaning: ईद के अवसर पर रखा जाने वाला नाम
in_hindi.long_meaning: बैरम नाम का अर्थ है ईद या त्योहार। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में ईद के अवसर पर बच्चों को दिया जाता है। यह नाम अरबी भाषा से आया है और इसका उपयोग ईद के महत्वपूर्ण त्योहार को मनाने के लिए किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: بیرم

in_pashto.long_meaning: بیرم نوم د عربی کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د عید یا جشن معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون په دودیزو کړو کې د عید الفطر یا عید الاضحیٰ د لمانځلو لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Bayram
in_english.meaning: Name related to Eid celebrations in Islamic cultures
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bayram originates from Arabic and is associated with Eid celebrations, specifically Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha. In various Islamic cultures, Bayram is used to signify these joyous occasions. The etymology of the name is linked to Arabic words meaning 'festival' or 'celebration'. Historically, the name has been used in different Muslim communities to commemorate significant religious events. Spiritually, Bayram symbolizes joy, unity, and devotion among Muslims.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Bayram" refers to a joyous and celebratory occasion, in the Islamic calendar, that marks the completion of the annual pilgrimage to Mecca, known as Hajj. During this time, Muslims around the world come together to honor the memory of Abraham, Ibrahim, and his family's devotion to God. The celebrations associated with Bayram, including family gatherings, communal feasts, and gift-giving, foster a sense of unity and solidarity among the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: Bayram is a reminder of the spiritual journey that every Muslim should embark upon in their lifetime, which is to make the pilgrimage to Mecca and strive to live a life that is pleasing to God. The spirit of Bayram emphasizes the importance of showing kindness, compassion, and gratitude to family, friends, and all of creation. This spiritual significance encourages Muslims to reflect on their relationship with God and to renew their commitment to following God's guidelines in their daily lives. By embodying the qualities of Bayram as a person who brings joy and delight to others, Muslims can contribute to their own spiritual growth and the wellbeing of their communities.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Joy, Delight" symbolizes A person who brings joy and delight to others. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Bayram serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of joy, delight.
